Ossido · 18

Serie Ossido — red lead oxide ground, cream and bone line, corner composition with the elevations opposite. The F40 below is the finished lot: fitted to A1 on its own drawn border, the words set INTO the title block the model drew. Every other sheet is a candidate — fitted the same way, left wordless; the type pass lands after the pick, into that sheet’s own block. Lot copy and print file on the Lot Board.

A1 native · F40

One sheet, twice. The F40 was reaching A1 by mirroring its own paper out of the band beside each edge - and that band held the border the model ruled, so the mirror copied the border back inward: a doubled rule along the bottom and a seam about 200 px in from the top and bottom trim. On the right it was worse, because the model ruled 0.24% of the width in from the sides and 1.07% of the height in from the top, so no amount of per-side padding could make that rectangle equidistant.

Rebuilt: the model's border is found as a spike in the ink profile - a ruled line stands 13 to 30 times above the paper baseline where the drawing's own dimension lines reach barely 2 - and medianed away, giving back the paper under it. Then the least new paper that reaches A1 goes on, grown from a real bare rectangle of this sheet's own margin and cross-dissolved into the join, and one line is ruled at an equal inset. 1% added on the right, 6% on the top, nothing cropped, nothing stretched, 9933 × 7016 exactly. Rule at 25 mm, clear of the drawing by 13 mm on the tightest side.

Free style fixed

One line, small gap - the blue TAV. II F40 as the measure. Where the sheet drew its own border that border IS the rule, and the paper is padded per side until it sits with an equal margin on all four; where it drew none, or drew one skewed, the band is wiped and one hand-ruled line goes in at an equal inset. Nothing cropped, nothing stretched, native A1 at 9933 × 7016.

Five · edges fixed

Five sheets made after the edge rule went in. Every one is exactly A1 - 9933 × 7016, ratio 1.4158 - with the paper running to all four edges and 0.0% white base measured on every edge. The white was never fixable by asking nicely: the models keep drawing a photograph of a sheet lying on a surface, so the finisher now FINDS the poster inside the render, crops to it, and refuses to write a hero at all if any edge still carries a white band.

New style · 18

Eighteen cars in the locked style, finished: graphite, corner composition, hand-ruled frame, full bleed to a straight edge, landscape. Each one fitted to true A1 and dressed with its marque, model, subtitle, specification, dimensions, folio numeral and imprint. The specification label is a wash of the sheet's own ground, the way a spec label was pasted onto a works drawing - the sheets are too dense to leave a clean quarter empty.

Blue · 6

Six new cars drawn into the collection that is already live: classic cyanotype, deep prussian blue, crisp white line, flat orthographic plate with no perspective view. Same finisher, but it reads the ground first - white ink on blue, and the label is a deeper blue rather than a pale box.

Free style · 36

Thirty-six heroes with no brief at all: twelve grounds and media, three cars each, and the composition rotated as well so the spread covers layout as much as look. Anything here can be promoted to a collection by moving one sentence.

First two heroes

Two lot heroes, finished. Landscape, graphite, corner composition, full bleed to a straight edge, fitted to true A1 at 9933 × 7016 - and then our type set into the space the drawing left, measured rather than assumed. The Jaguar carries its real wordmark; the Mercedes marque is typeset, which is an open item.

The candidates behind them

Two per car. The other one of each pair is untouched and can be finished the same way in a minute if you prefer it.

Frames & graphite

Your read on the last round: the graphite sheet worked because its outer line carried the same wear as the paper, and the Mustang gave itself away because its frame was a perfect rectangle. So the frame gets its own axis here - four ways to draw it, against the untouched baseline, on both stack sheets.

Ford Mustang 2+2 Fastback

Jaguar E-Type Series 1 3.8

Graphite + hand-ruled frame

The two things you singled out, combined and taken across the roster: soft pencil with smudged shading and eraser marks, inside a frame drawn with a ruling pen that skips and breaks where the paper is worn.

Reserved space

You spotted the empty lower left of the Corner sheet as room to work in. Here the prompt asks for it outright - a quarter of the sheet kept bare, no lines crossing it, waiting for our type.

Depth explorations

The depth prompt, opened up. Two axes. Composition is where the shaded three-quarter hero sits and what surrounds it - six of them, on four cars. Treatment is what the sheet is drawn with and on - four of them, run on the baseline composition so the axes stay readable apart. Everything else - the car sentence, the paper sentence, the no-text rule - is identical throughout.

Archivio

Collection two. Aged ivory paper, dark sepia ink, one muted red accent - the v1-warm-archive look from the locked style round, held fixed while the car changes. Each model is shown at three levels of paint: none, the side elevation only, or side plus plan. Title blocks are left empty on purpose - every word on a finished sheet is set by us afterwards.
